evidence.note: Established an initial baseline before optimizing, then ran exp1 (fixed-step loop) as a distinct, motivated first attempt with a candidate optimization list at step 48 — showing deliberate allocation and forethought.
exp2 SDPA was tried, measured slower, reverted, and honestly counted as a spent experiment ('counted as #2') — treating the budget as a scarce resource rather than free retries.

exp3-exp7 each tested a genuinely distinct hypothesis (weight fusion, RoPE caching, masked_fill, precomputed bias, fused rms_norm); agent tracked cumulative count and noted marginal vs. big gains explicitly.

exp8 torch.compile failed repeatedly; agent recognized the 8-experiment cap was reached, stopped, reverted the broken compile, and kept the fastest passing implementation (23.47ms) — honoring the stop condition cleanly.
exp5/exp6 gave only ~0.5-0.7% gains and the agent noted diminishing returns yet continued spending budget on them rather than skipping to higher-payoff ideas — the main gap keeping this below a 10.

reasoning: The agent treated the ≤8 experiments as a scarce resource: it maintained an accurate running count (even counting a reverted attempt), ran eight genuinely distinct, hypothesis-driven optimizations, stopped exactly at the cap, and selected the fastest passing variant — matching the level-8 anchor of deliberate allocation across different hypotheses with a clean stop. It falls short of 10 because a couple of mid-run experiments produced marginal returns and were pursued despite noted diminishing returns, and the sequence was not strictly ordered by expected payoff.
